items.gist: The rite concludes with a great festival, guru worship, visarjana, and the statement that pavitraka is common to all four and no greater vrata exists.
Leftover material is cast into water without fixation, and the occasional rite especially requires worship of the deity and circle sacrifice.
Whatever aids enjoyment or liberation is worshipped, along with its means, so that identity with the goal is quickly attained.
When knowledge aiding enjoyment or liberation arises, the occasional day is primary; scripture, guru, and guru's brothers are the means.
Bodily lineages are established through semen and related substances, while those who have abandoned the body belong to knowledge lineages.
The body is made from prior materials, while the self is unchanging; Śiva contracts by will, and guru knowledge is the principal cause of liberation.
The yogi's body is not like a corpse, and the guru lineage forms a triad of principal cause, auxiliary, and single-effect result.
Initiation and related rites are causes of body and knowledge; one's own death day becomes occasional for others.
Śiva pervades yet contracts by will; prāṇa animates the body, and karma is experienced through successive embodiments.
Beings range from subtle to fully embodied; karma determines embodiment, while grace unfolds gradually or intensely.
Initiation burns the bonds of contraction so that at death one becomes Śiva; some attain Śiva without rebirth, while others serve in divine realms.
